drivingQuestion: Under what conditions may one slaughter or cut with a knife that carries a prohibition, and what remedy — peeling, rinsing or purging — does its use require?
outcomeNote: Each difficulty is answered: the knife of idol worship is a case with no residue, both versions of the peel/rinse dispute are given a shared premise, and the halakha is fixed that a tereifa knife needs only cold water

segments.he: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ: סַכִּין שֶׁל עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה מוּתָּר לִשְׁחוֹט בָּהּ, וְאָסוּר לַחְתּוֹךְ בָּהּ בָּשָׂר. מוּתָּר לִשְׁחוֹט בָּהּ – מְקַלְקֵל הוּא, וְאָסוּר לַחְתּוֹךְ בָּהּ בָּשָׂר – מְתַקֵּן הוּא.
segments.en: § «Rav Naḥman says that Rabba bar Avuh says:» With regard to «a knife» used «for idol worship,» it is «permitted to slaughter» an animal «with it, but» it is «prohibited to cut meat with it.» It is «permitted to slaughter» an animal «with it» because slaughtering it «is a destructive» action vis-à-vis the animal, which is worth more when it is alive. «But» it is «prohibited to cut meat with it,» because once the animal is slaughtered, cutting it «is a constructive» action that renders the meat manageable.

segments.he: אָמַר רָבָא: פְּעָמִים שֶׁהַשּׁוֹחֵט אָסוּר – בִּמְסוּכֶּנֶת, וּמְחַתֵּךְ מוּתָּר – בְּאַטְמֵי דְּקָיְימָן לְקוּרְבָּנָא.
segments.en: «Rava said:» There are «times when» it is «prohibited» for «one who slaughters» an animal to use a knife used for idol worship, e.g., «in» the case of an animal that is in «danger,» meaning that it is about to die. If he does not slaughter the animal it would become an unslaughtered carcass and depreciate in value. «And» there are times when it is «permitted» for «one who cuts» meat to use a knife of idol worship, e.g., «in» the case of an animal whose «thighs are intended to» be sent as «a gift» to a person of stature. Cutting it into pieces would render it unfit for this purpose, thereby diminishing its value.

The Gemara challenges: «And derive» that «it» is prohibited to use a knife used for idol worship, not because benefit from it is prohibited, but «due to» the residue of «fat of forbidden» carcasses on the knife.
The Gemara rejects that possibility: Rav Naḥman is referring «to» the case of «a new» knife on which there is no residue.

segments.he: חֲדָשָׁה, בֵּין לְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בֵּין לְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, מְשַׁמְּשֵׁי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה הֵן, וּמְשַׁמְּשֵׁי עֲבוֹדָה זָרָה אֵינָן אֲסוּרִין עַד שֶׁיֵּעָבֵדוּ! אִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא, דִּפְסַק בֵּיהּ גְּוָוזָא לַעֲבוֹדָה זָרָה, וְאִיבָּעֵית אֵימָא, בִּישָׁנָה שֶׁלִּיבְּנָהּ בָּאוּר.
segments.en: The Gemara challenges: If it is «a new» knife, «both» according «to Rabbi Yishmael and» according «to Rabbi Akiva,» who disagreed about whether an idol is forbidden from the moment that one crafts it or from the moment that one worships it, a knife is merely in the category of «accessories of idol worship, and accessories of idol worship are forbidden only after they are» used for idol «worship.» The Gemara explains: «If you wish, say» that the reference is to a case «where he cut a branch [gevaza] for idol worship with» the knife, which leaves no residue. «And if you wish, say» instead that Rav Naḥman is referring «to» the case of «an old» knife «that he burned until» it became «white hot in the fire,» and therefore, there is no residue on the knife.

segments.he: אִתְּמַר: הַשּׁוֹחֵט בְּסַכִּין שֶׁל גּוֹיִם, רַב אָמַר: קוֹלֵף, וְרַבָּה בַּר בַּר חָנָה אָמַר: מֵדִיחַ. לֵימָא בְּהָא קָמִיפַּלְגִי, דְּמָר סָבַר: בֵּית הַשְּׁחִיטָה צוֹנֵן, וּמָר סָבַר: בֵּית הַשְּׁחִיטָה רוֹתֵחַ.
segments.en: § «It was stated:» With regard to «one who slaughters» an animal «with the knife of gentiles, Rav says: He peels» off a layer of the flesh from the place on the animal where the knife touched the flesh and the forbidden residue on the knife was absorbed. «And Rabba bar bar Ḥana says: He rinses» the place where the knife touched the flesh. The Gemara suggests: «Let us say» that «they disagree about this, that» one «Sage,» Rabba bar bar Ḥana, «holds: The area of the slaughter» on the throat «is cold» and does not absorb the forbidden residue, and therefore rinsing is sufficient. «And» one «Sage,» Rav, «holds: The area of the slaughter» on the throat «is hot» and therefore it absorbs the forbidden residue.

segments.he: לָא, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא בֵּית הַשְּׁחִיטָה רוֹתֵחַ הוּא; מַאן דְּאָמַר קוֹלֵף – שַׁפִּיר, וּמַאן דְּאָמַר מֵדִיחַ – אַיְּידֵי דִּטְרִידִי סִימָנִין לְאַפּוֹקֵי דָּם לָא בָּלְעִי.
segments.en: The Gemara rejects that suggestion: «No,» it is possible «that everyone» holds that «the area of the slaughter» on the throat «is hot.» For «the one who says» that «he peels» off a layer, it works out «well, and the one who says» that «he rinses» the place where the knife touched the flesh holds that «since the two organs that must be severed in ritual slaughter [simanim],» i.e., the windpipe and the gullet, «are occupied» with «discharging blood, they do not absorb» the residue.

segments.he: אִיכָּא דְּאָמְרִי, דְּכוּלֵּי עָלְמָא בֵּית הַשְּׁחִיטָה צוֹנֵן. מַאן דְּאָמַר מֵדִיחַ – שַׁפִּיר, מַאן דְּאָמַר קוֹלֵף – אַגַּב דּוּחְקָא דְסַכִּינָא בָּלַע.
segments.en: «There are» those «who say that everyone» holds that «the area of the slaughter» on the throat «is cold.» For «the one who says» that «he rinses» the place where the knife touched the flesh, it works out «well, and the one who says» that «he peels» off a layer holds that although that area is cold, «due to the pressure of the knife» on the throat, the flesh «absorbs» the residue.

segments.he: סַכִּין טְרֵיפָה, פְּלִיגִי בַּהּ רַב אַחָא וְרָבִינָא, חַד אָמַר: בְּחַמִּין, וְחַד אָמַר: בְּצוֹנֵן, וְהִלְכְתָא: אֲפִילּוּ בְּצוֹנֵן, וְאִי אִיכָּא בְּלִיתָא דִּפְרָסָא לְמִיכְפְּרֵיהּ, לָא צְרִיךְ.
segments.en: § «With regard to a knife» with which an animal that is «a tereifa» was slaughtered, «Rav Aḥa and Ravina disagree. One says:» One purges it «in hot» water to remove the absorptions from the tereifa, «and one says:» One rinses it «in cold» water, and that is sufficient. «And the halakha» is: One may rinse it «even in cold» water. «And if there is a tattered» piece «of a curtain» with which «to wipe» the knife, «one need not» rinse it.

segments.he: וּלְמַאן דְּאָמַר בְּחַמִּין, מַאי טַעְמָא? מִשּׁוּם דְּקָא בָלְעָה אִיסּוּרָא? דְּהֶיתֵּירָא נָמֵי בָּלְעָה אֵבֶר מִן הַחַי! אֵימַת בָּלְעָה? לְכִי חָיְימָא. אֵימַת קָא חָיְימָא? לְכִי גָמְרָה שְׁחִיטָה, הָהִיא שַׁעְתָּא הֶיתֵּירָא הֲוָה.
segments.en: «And according to the one who says» that one purges it «in hot» water, «what is the reason» that he must do so; is it «due to» the premise «that» the knife «absorbed forbidden» residue? That reasoning should not be limited to a case where he slaughtered a tereifa. A knife with «which» he slaughtered an animal that is «permitted» should «also» require purging, because «it absorbed» residue from «the limb from a living» animal before the slaughter was completed. The Gemara answers: «When» is there concern that the knife «absorbed» the residue? It is «when» the throat «grows warm. When does it grow warm?» It is «at» the point «when the slaughter is complete.» At «that moment, it is» already «permitted.»

moves.cueHe: אמר רב נחמן אמר רבה בר אבוה
moves.summary: A knife of idol worship may be used to slaughter but not to cut meat
moves.about: the ruling that a knife used for idol worship may be used to slaughter but not to cut meat

moves.summary: The rationale is supplied: slaughtering is destructive, cutting meat is constructive
moves.about: the rationale of the ruling — slaughtering is a destructive act vis-à-vis the animal while cutting the meat is a constructive one, so only the latter is a forbidden benefit

moves.summary: Rava carries the destructive/constructive criterion to converse cases: a dying animal, thighs meant as a gift
moves.about: extending the destructive/constructive criterion beyond slaughter and cutting — slaughtering an animal about to die is forbidden and cutting thighs set aside as a gift is permitted

moves.summary: The prohibition on cutting should follow from the forbidden fat residue, not from benefit of idol worship
moves.about: the prohibition on cutting meat with the knife should follow from the forbidden fat residue on it rather than from the prohibition of benefit from idol worship

moves.summary: Rav Naḥman speaks of a new knife, which bears no residue
moves.about: Rav Naḥman speaks of a new knife, on which there is no forbidden residue

moves.cueHe: חדשה, בין לרבי ישמעאל בין לרבי עקיבא
moves.summary: A new knife is only an accessory of idol worship, and accessories are forbidden only once used in worship
moves.about: a new knife is a mere accessory of idol worship, and accessories are forbidden only once they have actually been used in worship, so the answer בחדשה cannot stand

moves.cueHe: איבעית אימא, דפסק ביה גווזא לעבודה זרה
moves.summary: The knife was used to cut a branch for idol worship — used in worship, yet with no fat residue
moves.about: the case is one where he cut a branch for idol worship with the knife — it has been used in worship yet carries no fat residue

moves.summary: Alternatively an old knife heated white hot in fire, so no residue remains
moves.about: alternatively the case is an old knife that was heated white hot in fire, so no residue remains on it

moves.summary: It is floated that they disagree over whether the area of the slaughter is hot or cold
moves.about: Rabba bar bar Ḥana's ruling that one who slaughters with a gentile's knife merely rinses the place

moves.summary: Rav and Rabba bar bar Ḥana on slaughtering with a gentile's knife: peel off the flesh, or merely rinse it
moves.about: Rav's ruling that one who slaughters with a gentile's knife peels off a layer of flesh

moves.cueHe: לא, דכולי עלמא בית השחיטה רותח הוא
moves.summary: The floated account is rejected: all may hold the area of the slaughter is hot
moves.about: rejecting the suggested account of the dispute: everyone may hold that the area of the slaughter is hot

moves.summary: On the shared hot premise, peeling is straightforward and rinsing works because the simanim are busy discharging blood
moves.about: why rinsing suffices even on the hot view — the simanim are occupied discharging blood and so do not absorb

moves.summary: A second version: all hold the area is cold, and peeling is required because the knife's pressure makes the flesh absorb
moves.about: a second version of the anonymous account of the dispute, on which everyone holds the area of the slaughter is cold

moves.cueHe: סכין טריפה, פליגי בה רב אחא ורבינא
moves.summary: Rav Aḥa and Ravina dispute whether a tereifa knife is purged in hot water or rinsed in cold
moves.about: the halakha follows the view that cold water suffices for a knife used on a tereifa, and wiping with a rag dispenses with even that

moves.summary: The halakha: even cold water suffices, and wiping with a rag dispenses with even that
moves.about: how a knife used to slaughter a tereifa is purged — in hot water or by rinsing in cold water

moves.summary: What is the reason of the one who requires hot water?
moves.about: why purging in hot water should be required for a knife used on a tereifa

moves.summary: A candidate reason is floated: because the knife absorbed forbidden matter
moves.about: if absorption of forbidden matter is the reason, a knife used on a permitted animal should also need purging, since it absorbed from a limb of a living animal before the slaughter was complete

moves.cueHe: דהיתירא נמי בלעה אבר מן החי
moves.summary: Then a knife used on a permitted animal should also need purging, having absorbed from a limb of a living animal
moves.about: the knife absorbs only once the throat grows warm, which happens only when the slaughter is complete — at which moment the flesh is already permitted

moves.summary: Absorption occurs only once the throat warms, which is when the slaughter is complete and the flesh is already permitted
